data.title: Economic Growth Rose Slightly to Moderately in Most Fed Districts, Beige Book Shows
data.description:
02:26 PM EST, 11/25/2026 (MT Newswires) -- There was only slight to moderate growth in eight of the 12 Federal Reserve districts, with no change in the other four districts, the Federal Reserve's most recent Beige Book update released Wednesday showed.

"Consumer spending was little changed, as households remained price sensitive and were increasingly selective in discretionary purchases," according to the Beige Book summary, also noting softer auto sales due to higher fuel prices and interest rates.

Manufacturing activity was up modestly, but residential real estate activity weakened due to affordability challenges, the summary showed.

"Port volumes were slightly lower due to weather-driven disruptions, even as data center-related imports rose," the summary said. "Energy activity grew modestly but investment in this sector remained restrained by elevated geopolitical, policy, and cost uncertainties."

Employment levels were up only slightly, with firms noting stable payroll and hiring only to replace departing workers.

"Contacts across several sectors cited steady or rising labor demand, though many also described hesitancy to hire amid uncertainty and weakened consumer spending," the summary showed. "Labor supply generally remained stable, and while it was often relatively easy to find workers, persistent hiring difficulties continued for skilled and technical roles."

Wages and benefits were up moderately compared with only modest growth in the previous Beige Book report, with more growth in sectors where positions were hard to fill.

"Prices increased moderately overall, as in the prior reporting period," according to the summary. "Contacts across a range of sectors reported sustained cost pressure from energy, transportation, healthcare, insurance, and tariff-related expenses."

Further increases in both expenses and prices are expected in the coming month, the Beige Book said.

data.title: Correction: Hutchmed's New Drug Application for Orphathys-Osimertinib Combination to Treat Lung Cancer Accepted for Review in China
data.description:
03:55 AM EST, 11/27/2026 (MT Newswires) -- (Corrects headline to fix a typographical error in "lung cancer.")

Hutchmed ( HCM ) said Thursday that China's National Medical Products Administration has accepted for review a new drug application seeking approval of an all-oral combination of Orpathys and Astrazeneca's (AZN) osimertinib as a treatment for patients with non-small cell lung cancer.

The application is supported by results from a phase 3 trial showing the combination extended median progression-free survival to 24.9 months from 13.8 months with osimertinib alone, reducing the risk of disease progression or death by 44%, the company said.

The study also demonstrated an overall survival benefit, extending median overall survival by 9.6 months, while maintaining a safety profile consistent with the known profiles of the two medicines, Hutchmed ( HCM ) said.

data.title: Alvotech Plans Appeal of US Block on its Biosimilar Autoimmune Drug

The US court also directed Johnson & Johnson ( JNJ ) to post a bond to cover losses Alvotech ( ALVO ) may suffer, if it is ultimately found that the injunction was wrongful.

data.title: Update: Wall Street Mixed as Inflation, GDP Data Reinforce Rate-Hike Bets
data.description:
04:41 PM EST, 11/25/2026 (MT Newswires) -- (Updates with market moves at the end of the day, and other changes, if any.)

Wall Street closed mixed Wednesday as accelerating inflation and stronger-than-expected economic growth reinforced expectations for a December interest rate hike.

The Nasdaq Composite fell 0.6% to 23,585.80 and the S&P 500 declined 0.3% to 7,182.78, the second straight drop for both indexes. The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 0.3% to 50,182.95, rising for a third consecutive session.

US markets will be closed on Thursday for the Thanksgiving holiday.

Among sectors, consumer discretionary and technology led the laggards, while materials was the top gainer.

The personal consumption expenditure price index advanced 3.8% annually in October, its joint highest level since May, while the core measure accelerated to its fastest pace in nearly three years, the Bureau of Economic Analysis said.

Separately, the BEA reported the US economy grew at the fastest pace in three years in the third quarter as consumer spending growth accelerated from initial expectations.

"A larger-than-expected upward revision to (third-quarter) GDP underscores the resilient nature of the domestic economy," Stifel Chief Economist Lindsey Piegza said in a note emailed to MT Newswires. "For the Fed, further affirmation of dangerously elevated inflation coupled with a strong baseline of growth should be more than enough justification to continue to push rates higher not only next month but further into the new year."

Treasury yields were lower, with the 10-year rate dropping 3.6 basis points to 4.87% and the two-year rate falling 1.9 basis points to 4.65%.

Nvidia ( NVDA ) was the worst performer on the Dow Wednesday, closing 3.9% lower.

The technology bellwether's credit rating could be downgraded by S&P Global Ratings within the next three months as the rating agency placed the company on CreditWatch with negative implications.

Technology stocks Sandisk ( SNDK ) , Micron Technology ( MU ) , Intel ( INTC ) and Advanced Micro Devices ( AMD ) also declined. Investors remained concerned about growth durability and profitability of artificial intelligence-linked companies.

In other corporate news, HP (HPQ) shares jumped nearly 12%, the top performer on the S&P 500. The computer manufacturer reported fiscal fourth-quarter results above Wall Street's estimates late Tuesday.

Deere's (DE) fiscal fourth-quarter earnings unexpectedly declined year over year, and it issued a full-year profit outlook below market estimates amid ongoing uncertainty in key end markets. The company's shares closed 4.4% higher.

Brent crude oil rose 3.4% to $94.48 a barrel in Wednesday late-afternoon trade, while West Texas Intermediate increased 2.5% to $84.10 a barrel.

Spot gold increased 0.5% to $3,574.17 per troy ounce, while silver rose 0.3% to $41.37 per ounce.

data.title: Robbyant Open-Sources LingBot-Map 2.0 and LingBot-Navi, Enabling Long-Term Spatial Memory and Autonomous Navigation for Robots
data.description:
New models reduce long-distance mapping drift by nearly 85% and reduce the need for redundant exploration across tasks, advancing Robbyant’s universal embodied AI brain.

SHANGHAI--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Robbyant, an embodied AI company within Ant Group, today announced the open-source release of LingBot-Map 2.0, a streaming 3D reconstruction model, and LingBot-Navi, a spatial-memory navigation model. Designed to solve long-distance mapping drift and cross-task amnesia, the models allow robots to build maps on the move, self-calibrate in real time, and navigate complex physical environments with increasing efficiency.

This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261126690702/en/

Autonomous mobility is essential for physical AI, from warehouse logistics to last-mile delivery. Yet current systems face two major bottlenecks: long-distance mapping accumulates drift that external correction tools fail to feed back into the model's internal memory, and isolated navigation models force robots to re-explore familiar spaces from scratch for every new task.

LingBot-Map 2.0: Correcting Internal Memory, Not Just Output Trajectories

Building on LingBot-Map 1.0 (released in April 2026), LingBot-Map 2.0 introduces native internal error correction during inference, eliminating the reliance on external place-recognition modules or pose-graph optimization backends.

Powered by Geometric Context Reshaping (GCR), a mechanism inspired by memory reconsolidation in the human brain, the model reuses extracted local geometry and realigns high-level historical memory without re-encoding images. Because GCR updates the model's internal memory layer rather than merely adjusting output trajectories, every correction anchors a reliable spatial reference for future movement. Performance is further bolstered by LingBot-Vision, Robbyant’s visual foundation model, which provides sub-pixel boundary detection to minimize geometric errors at the source.

Key Benchmark Highlights:

  • Real-Time Speed: Achieves 27.51 FPS inference speed on a single NVIDIA RTX 5090 GPU.
  • Near 85% Drift Reduction: In a long-distance VBR urban trajectory test covering 5.2 km and nearly 19,000 frames, the Average Trajectory Error (ATE) dropped from 31.12 meters in version 1.0 to 4.72 meters, a reduction of nearly 85%. This is more than twice as accurate as the best-performing external loop-closure solution (9.98 m).
  • Industry-Leading Accuracy: On the Oxford Spires and KITTI benchmarks, the ATE was reduced to 3.92 meters and 9.42 meters, respectively. Furthermore, the model secured first place across three dense 3D reconstruction benchmarks: CroCoDL, EuRoC, and Oxford.

LingBot-Navi: Accelerating Task Efficiency with Reusable Spatial Memory

Built on LingBot-Map 2.0’s 3D perception, LingBot-Navi introduces persistent spatial memory that carries over between missions. Instead of wiping its map after completing an action, the model retains object and location data, retrieving relevant context when given a natural language command to plan direct routes without redundant exploration.

With every operation, LingBot-Navi refines robots’ understanding of the environment, steadily increasing execution speed. It also supports on-device deployment, keeping user commands and scene data local for low latency and data privacy.

Key Benchmark Highlights:

  • Higher Task Success: In simulations where the model selects targets and navigation is executed by a simulator, LingBot-Navi achieved a 68.60% success rate on the GOAT-Bench subset, outperforming the best of six comparative methods by 10.36 percentage points. In fully end-to-end tests—where the model autonomously plans paths and directly drives movement execution—it reached 56.09% on GOAT-Bench and 32.36% on Robbyant’s proprietary dataset, reconstructed from 36 real-world captured sites.
  • Superior Path Efficiency: Success weighted by Path Length (SPL) measures both whether the robot reaches the target and whether the route is efficient: shorter paths with fewer detours receive higher scores. LingBot-Navi achieved SPL scores of 38.04% on GOAT-Bench and 26.35% on the proprietary evaluation dataset, improving over the best control results by 1.42 and 16.84 percentage points, respectively.
  • Zero-Retraining Gains: Simply upgrading the underlying mapping engine from LingBot-Map 1.0 to 2.0 boosted navigation success rates by 4.15 and 2.35 percentage points across two evaluation sets (with SPL gains of 1.89 and 1.97 percentage points)—proving that higher-precision reconstruction directly improves task completion without retraining the navigation model.

Together, LingBot-Map 2.0 and LingBot-Navi strengthen the capabilities of Robbyant’s universal embodied AI brain — from spatial perception to efficient navigation.

Technical reports, related code, the Pure Streaming model weights for LingBot-Map 2.0, the model weights for LingBot-Navi, and a dataset covering 511 real-world captured scenes are now fully open-sourced to support further community research:

  • LingBot-Map 2.0

data.title: The Coca-Cola Company and Gutsche Family Investments Close on Sale of Controlling Interest in Coca-Cola Beverages Africa to Coca-Cola HBC AG
data.description:
ATLANTA & ZUG, Switzerland--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- The Coca-Cola Company ( KO ) and Gutsche Family Investments (GFI) have completed the sale of a 75% controlling interest in Coca-Cola Beverages Africa Pty. Ltd. (CCBA) to Coca-Cola HBC AG ( CCHBF ).

The proposed transaction was first announced in October 2025. The companies closed on Nov. 27 after receiving all necessary regulatory approvals in Africa.

Coca-Cola and Coca-Cola HBC ( CCHBF ) have a separate option agreement providing Coca-Cola HBC ( CCHBF ) the opportunity to acquire the remaining 25% stake in CCBA held by Coca-Cola within a six-year period.

CCBA is the largest Coca-Cola bottler in Africa, operating in 14 countries. Following completion of the deal, Coca-Cola HBC ( CCHBF ) is the second-largest Coca-Cola bottler globally by volume, extending its footprint to 43 markets and serving approximately 1.2 billion consumers across Europe and Africa.

Advancing Coca-Cola's Refranchising Strategy

The completion of the transaction marks another significant milestone in Coca-Cola's ongoing strategy to refranchise company-owned and controlled bottling operations.

“This transaction reflects the strength of the Coca-Cola system and our long-term commitment to building locally led, world-class bottling operations,” said Henrique Braun, CEO of The Coca-Cola Company ( KO ). “CCBA has established a strong foundation across Africa, and Coca-Cola HBC ( CCHBF ) brings proven capabilities, deep market expertise and a successful track record of investing for sustainable growth.”

Luis Felipe Avellar, president of the Africa operating unit of The Coca Cola Company ( KO ), said, “We are confident this combination will create new opportunities for customers, consumers and communities across the continent. Coca-Cola HBC ( CCHBF ) is a strong, valued partner that has the ability to grow our business in Africa.”

The Gutsche family will remain connected to the Coca-Cola system and Africa through its ownership stake in Coca-Cola HBC ( CCHBF ).

Strengthening Coca-Cola HBC’s Presence in Africa

The acquisition builds on Coca-Cola HBC’s origins in Nigeria 75 years ago and its expansion into Egypt in 2022. Following completion of the acquisition, Coca-Cola HBC ( CCHBF ) now represents approximately two-thirds of Africa’s total Coca-Cola system volume and serves more than half of the continent’s population. The combination creates a stronger platform to share capabilities, invest in people and infrastructure, and drive sustainable, profitable growth.

Zoran Bogdanovic, CEO of Coca-Cola HBC ( CCHBF ), said: “Today we mark a historic milestone as we complete the acquisition of CCBA. Africa is where Coca-Cola HBC ( CCHBF ) began 75 years ago, and this acquisition significantly strengthens our presence across this incredible continent, creating a strong platform for sustainable, profitable growth. Our listing on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange this week further underlines our long-term commitment to South Africa and the broader African continent.

“CCBA is a high-quality business with strong market positions, deep local knowledge and talented people. We are very pleased to welcome our new colleagues to Coca-Cola HBC ( CCHBF ). Together, we will invest in our leading 24/7 portfolio, our bespoke capabilities and our passionate people to capture the significant opportunities ahead.

“I would like to thank The Coca-Cola Company ( KO ) and the Gutsche family for their trust and partnership, and our teams across CCBA, Coca-Cola HBC ( CCHBF ) and the wider Coca-Cola system for their commitment in completing this transaction. We look forward to working together to drive joint success.”

As part of the transaction, Coca-Cola sold 41.52% of its 66.52% stake in CCBA to Coca-Cola HBC ( CCHBF ), while Coca-Cola HBC ( CCHBF ) acquired the 33.48% stake held by GFI.

Rothschild & Co. acted as sole financial adviser to Coca-Cola. Goldman Sachs Bank Europe SE, Amsterdam Branch and UBS AG London Branch acted as financial advisers to Coca-Cola HBC ( CCHBF ). Nomura International acted as sole financial adviser to GFI.

About The Coca-Cola Company ( KO )

The Coca-Cola Company ( KO ) is a total beverage company with products sold in more than 200 countries and territories. Our company’s purpose is to refresh the world and make a difference. We sell multiple billion-dollar brands across several beverage categories worldwide. Our portfolio of sparkling soft drink brands includes Coca-Cola, Sprite and Fanta. Our water, sports, coffee and tea brands include Dasani, smartwater, vitaminwater, Topo Chico, BODYARMOR, Powerade, Costa, Georgia, Fuze Tea, Gold Peak and Ayataka. Our juice, value-added dairy and plant-based beverage brands include Minute Maid, Simply, innocent, Del Valle, fairlife and Santa Clara. We’re constantly transforming our portfolio, from reducing sugar in our drinks to bringing innovative new products to market. We seek to positively impact people’s lives, communities and the planet through water replenishment, packaging recycling, sustainable sourcing practices and carbon emissions reductions across our value chain. Together with our bottling partners, we employ more than 700,000 people, helping bring economic opportunity to local communities worldwide. Learn more at www.coca-colacompany.com and follow us on Instagram, Facebook and LinkedIn.

About Coca-Cola HBC AG ( CCHBF )

Coca-Cola HBC ( CCHBF ) is a growth-focused consumer packaged goods business and strategic bottling partner of The Coca-Cola Company ( KO ). Our business was founded in Nigeria in 1951, and this year we celebrate our 75th anniversary. We open up moments that refresh us all, by creating value for our stakeholders and supporting the socio-economic development of the communities in which we operate. With a vision to be the leading 24/7 beverage partner, we offer drinks for all occasions around the clock. Following the completion of our acquisition of a majority stake in Coca-Cola Beverages Africa on 27 November 2026, we work together with our customers to serve more than 1.2 billion consumers across 43 markets in Europe and Africa.

Our portfolio is one of the strongest, broadest and most flexible in the beverage industry, with consumer-leading brands across the sparkling, adult sparkling, juice, water, sport, energy, ready-to-drink tea, coffee, and premium spirits categories, with snacks as an additional offering. Our products include Coca-Cola, Coca-Cola Zero Sugar, Fanta, Sprite, Schweppes, Kinley, Costa Coffee, Caffè Vergnano, Valser, Romerquelle, Dasani and other water brands, FuzeTea, Powerade, Cappy, Monster Energy, Finlandia Vodka, The Macallan, Jack Daniel's and Plazma. data.title: XPENG Accelerates Global Physical AI Expansion at the 2026 Guangzhou International Automobile Exhibition
data.description:
• In a world-first, XPENG’s humanoid robot IRON hosted an automotive press conference, announcing the establishment of XPENG’s Hong Kong R&D Centre, dedicated to humanoid robotics and general-purpose intelligence. IRON is set to begin its international deployment in the second half of 2027.
  • XPENG ( XPEV ) is on track to surpass 100,000 annual overseas vehicle sales for the first time in 2026 and aims to more than double its overseas sales in 2027.
  • XPENG ( XPEV ) plans to introduce five new models across overseas markets in 2027, including the New P7, which will launch in Europe, its first overseas market, in the second quarter of 2027. The next wave of expansion begins with the L05’s launch in Thailand in December 2026.
  • XPENG ( XPEV ) plans to deploy four X-Energy megawatt charging stations across three continents within three months, accelerating the global expansion of its charging infrastructure.
  • XPENG ( XPEV ) plans to begin the overseas rollout of its advanced driver-assistance system in the first half of 2027, with a global launch of its Robotaxi targeted for 2027.

GUANGZHOU, China, Nov. 27, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- XPENG ( XPEV ) today unveiled the next phase of its global Physical AI strategy at the 2026 Guangzhou Auto Show, outlining its 2027 expansion roadmap across AI vehicles, humanoid robotics and autonomous mobility. Key plans include the introduction of five new vehicle models across international markets, with Europe confirmed as the first overseas market for the New P7, alongside the planned overseas deployment of its humanoid robot IRON and the international introduction of its Robotaxi programme.

XPENG ( XPEV ) also announced the establishment of its Hong Kong R&D Centre, the company’s ninth R&D centre worldwide, alongside plans to expand its X-Energy megawatt charging infrastructure across three continents.

Building on XPENG AI Day 2026 earlier in the week, the exhibition brought together international media and partners to experience how XPENG ( XPEV ) is translating its Physical AI innovations into real-world applications.

Image: XPENG ( XPEV ) showcases its latest innovations in Physical AI at the 2026 Guangzhou Auto Show.
XPENG ( XPEV ) showcases its latest innovations in Physical AI at the 2026 Guangzhou Auto Show.

IRON Takes the Mic: From Stage to Showroom

At the Guangzhou Auto Show, IRON took centre stage to host XPENG’s press conference, introducing its capabilities and interacting with an international audience. Beyond the stage, multiple IRON humanoid robots took on customer-facing roles together for the first time, serving as sales assistants, receptionists and technology guides across XPENG’s exhibition booth. They welcomed visitors, introduced vehicles and answered product enquiries, demonstrating their potential for real-world retail applications.

During the press conference, IRON also announced the official establishment of XPENG’s Hong Kong R&D Centre, which will focus on humanoid robotics and general-purpose intelligence. Its key research areas include whole-body motion control, mobile manipulation, world models and embodied intelligence. Research will also span advanced algorithms, AI software and system architecture, and data engineering. Leveraging Hong Kong’s strong research ecosystem and technology talent, the new centre will further strengthen XPENG’s global R&D capabilities in Physical AI.

Image: XPENG’s humanoid robots IRON demonstrate their service capabilities, welcoming visitors and introducing vehicles at the 2026 Guangzhou Auto Show.
XPENG’s humanoid robots IRON demonstrate their service capabilities, welcoming visitors and introducing vehicles at the 2026 Guangzhou Auto Show.

After eight years of research and development, IRON is moving beyond technology demonstrations towards real-world service applications. In the first quarter of 2027, IRON will begin its first showroom assignments at XPENG ( XPEV ) retail locations in China, gaining practical experience in everyday retail environments. In the second half of 2027, XPENG ( XPEV ) plans to extend IRON’s deployment internationally, starting with its overseas showroom network.

“The true value of Physical AI lies not in what technology can demonstrate on stage, but in what it can deliver in the real world,” said He Xiaopeng, Chairman and CEO of XPENG ( XPEV ). “IRON’s transition from research and development to everyday service environments represents an important step in this journey. We believe the next wave of AI innovation will increasingly take place in the physical world, transforming how people move, work and interact with technology. In 2027, we plan to accelerate the global deployment of our AI vehicles, humanoid robots and Robotaxis, turning technological innovation into tangible value for customers around the world.”

Image: He Xiaopeng, Chairman and CEO of XPENG ( XPEV ), joins humanoid robot IRON on stage at XPENG’s press conference at the 2026 Guangzhou Auto Show.
He Xiaopeng, Chairman and CEO of XPENG ( XPEV ), joins humanoid robot IRON on stage at XPENG’s press conference at the 2026 Guangzhou Auto Show.

XPENG Accelerates Global Vehicle Expansion with Five New Models in 2027

XPENG’s international business is entering a new phase of growth, with annual overseas vehicle sales on track to surpass 100,000 units for the first time in 2026. In October alone, overseas deliveries reached a record 13,326 vehicles, representing a year-on-year increase of 166%.

XPENG’s global sales and service network now spans 83 countries and regions, with more than 1,300 retail stores worldwide. In Europe, cumulative deliveries have surpassed 10,000 vehicles in each of Denmark, Norway, France and Germany. XPENG ( XPEV ) also ranks as the best-selling Chinese automotive brand in Europe for battery-electric vehicles priced above €40,000 from January to October 2026, underscoring its strong position in the region’s premium EV market segment.

This momentum is underpinned by growing customer recognition and strong market performance across regions. XPENG ( XPEV ) ranked first for brand recommendation in the USCALE EV Satisfaction Study across Germany, Austria and Switzerland for two consecutive years, in 2025 and 2026, while the XPENG X9 became the first MPV to win the Luxury category of the German Car of the Year 2027 awards. The X9 also achieved segment-leading sales in several Asia-Pacific markets, while the XPENG GX secured more than 5,000 orders within a month of its introduction across multiple Middle Eastern and African markets.

XPENG’s next wave of international product expansion will begin in December 2026 with the launch of the XPENG L05, a spacious, intelligent five-seat SUV designed for families, in Thailand, its first overseas market. The model will then officially launch in Europe at the Brussels Motor Show in January 2027.

In 2027, XPENG ( XPEV ) plans to introduce five new vehicle models across key international markets, broadening its product portfolio to address a wider range of customer needs. Among them is the New P7, which will make its international market debut in Europe in the second quarter of 2027. Since its appearance at IAA Mobility 2025 in Munich, the model has attracted interest from European audiences, with its distinctive design earning the prestigious 2026 Red Dot Design Award.

“We aim to more than double our overseas vehicle sales in 2027 compared with 2026,” said Alex, Vice President of XPENG International Business. “But our focus goes beyond sales growth and new vehicle launches. It is about understanding local customer needs, strengthening our local presence and building lasting relationships with customers and partners. These are the foundations for our long-term growth in international markets.”

Image: Alex, Vice President of XPENG International Business, shares XPENG’s global business updates and 2027 international expansion plans at the 2026 Guangzhou Auto Show.
Alex, Vice President of XPENG International Business, shares XPENG’s global business updates and 2027 international expansion plans at the 2026 Guangzhou Auto Show.

Accelerating the Global Rollout of X-Energy Megawatt Charging

Alongside its global vehicle expansion, XPENG ( XPEV ) is accelerating the deployment of its X-Energy megawatt charging infrastructure, with plans to expand its network across three continents by the end of 2026. Following the opening of its first X-Energy megawatt charging station in Hong Kong in September 2026, XPENG ( XPEV ) plans to deploy its second station in Hong Kong, Australia’s first megawatt charging station, and its first two X-Energy stations in Europe, located in Germany and the Netherlands, respectively.

Built on XPENG’s in-house-developed energy storage and ultra-fast charging technology, the X-Energy system can deliver up to 1,000 kW of peak power with a grid connection of no more than 240 kW. By using stored energy to boost charging output, the system reduces pressure on local power grids and facilitates the deployment of megawatt charging infrastructure in densely populated urban areas with limited grid capacity and space, while supporting the second-life use of retired EV batteries.

From Advanced Driver Assistance to Autonomous Mobility

Beyond expanding its vehicle portfolio, XPENG ( XPEV ) is accelerating the international introduction of its advanced driver-assistance technology. Building on large-scale public test rides at the Paris Motor Show, XPENG ( XPEV ) became the first Chinese automaker to offer public test rides of advanced urban driver-assistance technology at an overseas retail location, bringing its intelligent driving technology closer to everyday consumers.

Powered by the VLA 2.0 architecture, XPENG’s advanced driver-assistance system, NGP, is undergoing international testing and localisation ahead of a planned overseas rollout in the first half of 2027, subject to local validation, regulatory requirements and market readiness.

XPENG ( XPEV ) is also extending its Physical AI capabilities into autonomous mobility through YoYo-01, its purpose-built Robotaxi, which is undergoing Level 4 autonomous driving tests. Built on XPENG’s fully in-house-developed technology stack, including its Turing AI chips, VLA 2.0 model and autonomous driving software, YoYo-01 leverages a shared AI technology foundation spanning Level 2 driver assistance and Level 4 autonomous driving.

With a global launch targeted for 2027, XPENG ( XPEV ) aims to explore international opportunities in Robotaxi services, expanding the application of its AI technologies beyond private vehicles.

As XPENG ( XPEV ) enters its next phase of global growth, its international strategy is evolving beyond intelligent vehicles to encompass a broader ecosystem of Physical AI technologies. Through AI vehicles, humanoid robots and Robotaxis, XPENG ( XPEV ) aims to bring the benefits of AI into everyday life for people around the world.

About XPENG ( XPEV )

XPENG ( XPEV ) is a leading global Physical AI company, dedicated to bringing artificial intelligence into the physical world to reshape future mobility and smart living. Through in-house R&D, XPENG ( XPEV ) has developed a full-stack Physical AI architecture spanning Turing AI chips, world foundation models, and highly integrated software and hardware applications. data.title: Binance says customer withdrawals are fully restored, four weeks after the $6.3 billion hack
data.description:
Binance, the world's largest crypto trading platform, said it has fully lifted the suspension on customer withdrawals that began after a $6.3 billion hack in late October.

"Our withdrawal recovery work is completed and the withdrawal suspension from the October security incident has been fully lifted," the exchange said in an announcement dated Nov. 26. Withdrawals are how customers move their crypto off the exchange to wallets of their own.

The trouble began on Oct. 29, when Binance said a hack that day affected about $6.3 billion in assets, the biggest crypto hack on record, and that around $3 billion of it was frozen. The exchange immediately stopped withdrawals on several blockchain networks as a precaution and  began bringing them back in stages on Nov. 1, starting with Bitcoin and other limited set of networks and coins.

Co-CEO Yi He promised within hours to cover "all hacking losses." On Oct. 31, Binance said it had put back 90% of the stolen crypto, paying from company money and from its SAFU fund, an emergency reserve it keeps for cases like this. By Nov. 3, it said the figure was 98% of the $6.34 billion affected.

Binance's first look suggested that an engineer's laptop was compromised, which let an attacker into part of its systems and send out withdrawals nobody had approved. In a report on Nov. 3, it said hackers had used fake job interviews, malicious software and compromised internal AI tools to reach the systems that control its wallets.

Private blockchain forensics firms blamed North Korea-linked entities for the exploit. TRM Labs, which tracks crypto crime, tied the attack to a North Korean group called TraderTraitor. The FBI has also pointed to North Korea.

A few networks are still paused, but Binance says that is not related to the hack.

“Withdrawals for a small number of networks are temporarily paused while they undergo maintenance or planned upgrades,” the company said. It added that the pause affects a very small share of regular traffic and that such suspensions are standard practice when external conditions require them.

The company said delays can also originate on the networks themselves and directed users to its network status page. It did not specify which networks were affected.

Binance said customer money is safe.

"As we have shared, all assets remain fully backed and accounted for," it said, adding that users can check on its Proof of Reserves website that their assets are backed at least 1:1, meaning for every dollar a user holds, Binance holds at least a dollar.

It also warned that scammers often show up after events like this. Binance said it will never contact a user to "speed up withdrawals," offer "priority processing," or move assets into a "Binance vault." It said it will never ask for a password, a two-factor code or a seed phrase, which is the set of words that unlocks a crypto wallet.

The exchange asked users to trust only its official channels.

SINGAPORE, Nov. 26, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Gene Solutions today announced that Singapore's Health Sciences Authority (HSA) has approved the registration application of SPOT-MAS 10 as a Class C in vitro diagnostic (IVD) medical device.

Based on the Singapore Medical Device Register records as of 25 November 2026, SPOT-MAS 10 is the first blood-based multi-cancer screening test kit registered as an IVD in Singapore.

The Class C registration by Singapore's HSA, a WHO-recognized Stringent Regulatory Authority, marks an important regulatory milestone for SPOT-MAS 10 and may support future regulatory and compliance engagement with health authorities in other jurisdictions.

"HSA registration is a defining milestone for SPOT-MAS 10," said Dr. Nguyen Hoai Nghia, CEO and Co-founder of Gene Solutions. "It brings together the reagents, multi-omic analytical software and machine-learning capabilities developed through years of scientific research, prospective validation and real-world implementation. The registration provides a regulated IVD product pathway and an important foundation for broader regulatory and laboratory partnerships."

SPOT-MAS 10 is a qualitative in vitro diagnostic test performed on plasma derived from a single direct-draw venous whole blood specimen. The registered product comprises reagents and analytical software that analyze circulating cell-free DNA methylation and fragmentomic signatures using a machine-learning-based algorithm to detect a cancer-associated signal and predict its likely tissue of origin.

The registered intended use covers five common cancers, comprising breast, lung, liver, colorectal and gastric cancers, and five aggressive, less common cancers that currently lack standard screening methods: ovarian, pancreatic, esophageal, endometrial and head-and-neck cancers.

SPOT-MAS 10 is intended as an adjunctive screening test for asymptomatic adults aged 40 years or older who are at elevated risk for cancers within the scope of the assay.

A positive result is not a cancer diagnosis and should be followed by physician-directed diagnostic evaluation based on the predicted tissue of origin, the individual's risk factors and standard clinical practice.

A negative result does not rule out cancer. Individuals should continue all guideline-recommended cancer screening and routine medical care.

SPOT-MAS 10 does not replace standard-of-care cancer screening and is not intended for individuals with signs or symptoms suggestive of cancer, those undergoing diagnostic evaluation for a suspected malignancy, or individuals with a currently known malignancy.

Class C is a moderate-to-high-risk category under Singapore's risk-based medical-device framework. HSA is recognized by the World Health Organization as a Stringent Regulatory Authority for Class C and Class D IVDs. Singapore also attained WHO Maturity Level 4, the highest level under WHO's benchmarking framework for medical-device regulatory systems. These recognitions apply to Singapore's regulatory authority and do not constitute WHO review, prequalification or endorsement of SPOT-MAS 10.

In May 2026, SPOT-MAS 10 received Breakthrough Device Designation from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration, marking another regulatory milestone in the product's development. The designation facilitates more interactive engagement with the FDA during development and review. It is not FDA approval, clearance or marketing authorization, and SPOT-MAS 10 remains subject to future FDA regulatory review.

The scientific evidence supporting SPOT-MAS has continued to develop through clinical validation and real-world studies across Asia. The prospective K-DETEK study evaluated SPOT-MAS in 9,024 asymptomatic adults aged 40 years or older across 75 hospitals in Vietnam.

More than 105,000 individuals have been tested with SPOT-MAS in routine clinical settings across 10 Asian countries, with findings presented at Gene Solutions' ESMO 2026 Industry Satellite Symposium in Spain. Earlier real-world data were presented at ASCO Breakthrough 2026 in Singapore and highlighted by the American Society of Clinical Oncology ahead of the meeting.

HSA Class C registration marks an important step in expanding access to multi-cancer early detection. Gene Solutions will work with laboratory and healthcare partners to support the clinical implementation of SPOT-MAS 10.

About Gene Solutions

Gene Solutions is a global biotechnology company advancing precision cell-free DNA solutions across pregnancy care (triSure), cancer detection (SPOT-MAS), and precision oncology (K-TRACK, K-4CARE). By combining multi-omic science, data intelligence and a scalable technology platform, Gene Solutions brings world-class genomics closer to clinicians and patients, expanding access to clinically meaningful innovation around the world.

data.title: In The Economist's "The World Ahead 2027", XPENG CEO He Xiaopeng Outlines Humanoid Robotics Will Advance Through Hardware-Software Co-Evolution
data.description:
• Mr. He Xiaopeng, Chairman & CEO of XPENG ( XPEV ), outlines the technological breakthroughs needed to bring humanoid robots into mass production, positioning physical AI as the next frontier of technological innovation.
  • Mr. He Xiaopeng emphasizes: "Robots must be designed with a software mindset, but hardware must come first. Robots also need multiple speeds of thought, and the data they learn from needs variety, not merely volume."
  • Among the contributors to The World Ahead 2027, Mr. He Xiaopeng is the only China-based author, joining a distinguished lineup that includes Anthropic co-founder Jack Clark and Fields Medalist Terence Tao.

GUANGZHOU, China, Nov. 26, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Chairman & CEO of XPeng Inc. ( XPEV ) , a leading global Physical AI company, has contributed an article titled "Get Ready for Humanoid Robots"to The Economist's The World Ahead 2027, sharing his perspectives on the development of humanoid robots and the future of artificial intelligence in the physical world.

Published on November 18, 2026, the article explores the technological challenges and opportunities shaping the humanoid robotics industry, offering insights into how advanced general-purpose of humanoid robots could move beyond demonstrations and enter real-world applications.

Mr. He Xiaopeng emphasizes the importance of an integrated approach to humanoid robotics, stating: "Robots must be designed with a software mindset, but hardware must come first. Robots also need multiple speeds of thought, and the data they learn from needs variety, not merely volume." This philosophy highlights the need to develop hardware, software and data capabilities in tandem, building a comprehensive technological foundation that enables robots to perceive, reason, move and interact reliably in complex real-world environments. This full-stack approach is essential to accelerating the deployment and commercialization of humanoid robots.

Image: JSY_0175__23105257

XPENG's ( XPEV ) advanced general-purpose of humanoid robot IRON

Rethinking Intelligence: Humanoid Robots Need Multiple Speeds of Thought

One of the key insights into Mr. He Xiaopeng's article is that humanoid robots require fundamentally different layers of intelligence to operate effectively in the physical world.

"Rather than one all-purpose brain, humanoid robots will need several speeds of thought: ultra-fast models for motor control and split-second reflexes; fast models for motion and real-time interaction; slow models for reasoning and memory; separate models dedicated to safety." This vision is reflected in XPENG's ( XPEV ) Turing Physical AI Architecture (VLA 3.0), unveiled at XPENG AI Day 2026.

Designed to connect intelligence with physical execution, the architecture integrates three systems operating at different levels and speeds:

  • System 0 – Ultra-fast System: Integrates physical control into the AI loop, coordinating hardware, power, communication and execution while ensuring real-time body-state feedback and safe operation.
  • System 1 – Fast System: Powered by XPENG's ( XPEV ) VLA 2.0, enables real-time environmental perception and translates understanding into rapid, executable actions.
  • System 2 – Slow System: Combines vision-language-based task planning with an Agent Runtime state machine to support higher-level reasoning, complex task planning and coordinated decision-making.

Together, the three systems form a unified, continuous closed loop connecting cognition, action and physical feedback, enabling humanoid robots to think, respond and interact safely with the real world.

However, for general-purpose humanoid robots, progress is still needed in four areas: learning to move safely , handling tools and navigating different environments, acquiring and applying specialist knowledge and skills, and developing social and emotional intelligence to act appropriately in different situations.

2027: A New Milestone for Humanoid Robot Commercialization

In his contribution to The Economist, Mr. He Xiaopeng points to 2027 as a significant milestone for the humanoid robotics industry, anticipating the beginning of mass production of advanced general-purpose of humanoid robots. It will require not only advances in AI intelligence and mechanical capabilities, but also improvements in manufacturing efficiency, reliability, safety and cost competitiveness.

Image: MGP_1572__33919358

XPENG IRON

XPENG ( XPEV ) believes commercialization will progress in stages, starting with more structured commercial applications. XPENG’s humanoid robot IRON is designed to serve as a work partner and is scheduled to begin training as a store assistant at XPENG ( XPEV ) retail stores in Q1 2027. data.title: China's Huawei convicted in sprawling US criminal trial over Iran businessÂ
data.description:
NEW YORK, Nov 24 (Reuters) - Chinese telecommunications equipment maker Huawei was convicted by a jury in New York City on Tuesday in a sprawling US criminal case on charges that it deceived banks about its business in Iran and stole trade secrets from American companies.

The verdict came in a criminal case that began in 2018, with the US government the following year placing Huawei on a trade blacklist that restricted its access to US technology amid American concerns that Huawei posed national security risks.

The jury in Brooklyn federal court found Huawei guilty on 10 of the 12 criminal counts the company faced, including bank fraud, wire fraud, sanctions violations and conspiring to steal trade secrets. The jury acquitted Huawei of conspiring to obstruct justice and racketeering conspiracy, a charge alleging the company had acted as a criminal enterprise.

The trial lasted more than two months, with prosecutors calling more than 60 witnesses and the defense calling 15. It was not immediately clear what penalties Huawei will face when US District Judge Ann Donnelly sentences it on September 14, 2027. 

Reuters stories in 2012 and 2013 helped expose Huawei's activities in Iran and were discussed during the trial.

"After the media started questioning Huawei's operations in Iran, so did Huawei's banks," prosecutor Meredith Arfa told jurors during closing arguments in the case last week.

Brian Heberlig, a lawyer for Huawei, said the company was disappointed by the convictions but said the acquittal on the racketeering conspiracy charge vindicated its "good-faith compliance culture." 

"We fully expect to appeal," Heberlig told reporters. 

A spokesperson for the Brooklyn US Attorney's office, which brought the case, did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Neither the White House nor China's embassy in Washington immediately responded to requests for comment on the verdict. 

Asked how much the company may have to pay in penalties, Heberlig said it was premature to comment, but said the acquittal on the racketeering conspiracy charge could make a significant difference.

Experts have said the case did not undermine Huawei's business, as the company diversified and emerged as a key player in China's push for artificial intelligence.

FOUNDER'S DAUGHTER WAS DETAINED

In December 2018, Meng Wanzhou, Huawei's chief financial officer and daughter of the company's founder, was detained in Canada on a US warrant, prompting a diplomatic crisis involving the United States, China and Canada.

Meng had been secretly indicted on US charges of misleading an HSBC ( HSBC ) banker about Huawei's business in Iran, so the company could move dollars in and out of Iran in violation of American sanctions. Meng fought extradition to the US for nearly three years, before entering a deferred prosecution agreement and flying home to China to a hero's welcome. The charges against her were dropped.

Meng did not testify at trial, though an HSBC ( HSBC ) banker she met with in 2013 did testify.

The 2018 indictment alleged that Huawei misled HSBC ( HSBC ), Standard Chartered ( SCBFF ) and BNP Paribas about its business dealings in Iran. Prosecutors added new charges in 2020, including allegations that Huawei conspired to steal trade secrets from US technology companies over two decades.

THE PROSECUTION CASE

During the trial, prosecutors sought to prove that Huawei stole source code from Cisco Systems for its routers, stole wireless telecommunications company Quintel's antenna technology, and hired a professor to gain access to a circuit board developed by semiconductor company CNEX.

Jurors watched a video that, according to prosecutors, showed a Huawei employee slipping a piece of a T-Mobile testing robot into his backpack, and heard about a Huawei engineer sneaking into a Fujitsu ( FJTSF ) booth at a trade show to photograph a device. 

Prosecutors gave jurors a statement attached to Meng's deferred prosecution agreement in which she acknowledged that the company illegally conducted business in Iran. 

The defense argued that HSBC ( HSBC ) and the other banks knew about Huawei's business in Iran and were competing for Huawei's business.

Heberlig accused prosecutors during his closing argument of having "cherry-picked" a handful of disparate incidents to support their claim of a 20-year conspiracy. Heberlig said Huawei succeeded through "hard work, innovation, and investment in research and development." 

The company has more than 200,000 employees and operates in approximately 170 countries. 

(Additional reporting by Luc Cohen and Jonathan Stempel; Editing by Jonathan Spicer, Noeleen Walder and Will Dunham)

data.title: Taiwan's Stock Pickers Are Walking Out to Bet Their Own Money
data.description:
NEW YORK, Oct. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Fly On Wall Street News Commentary - Taiwan's benchmark stock index was up 62% this year, the best showing of any major equity gauge in the world, when Bloomberg reported on Oct. 16 that some of the island's professional fund managers and analysts are quitting their jobs to invest their own money. Strict rules keep them from trading the very stocks they pick for clients, and in a year when about one in ten stocks in the index has more than doubled, some have decided the trade-off is no longer worth it. Companies and funds mentioned in this article include: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited ( TSM ) [TSMC] , ASE Technology Holding Co., Ltd. ( ASX ) [ASE] , United Microelectronics Corporation ( UMC ) [UMC] , iShares MSCI Taiwan ETF , The Taiwan Fund, Inc. ( TWN ) .

Watching From Behind the Locker

Taiwan does not ban personal investing outright, but its asset-management code of conduct bars staff from trading a locally listed stock or a linked derivative within seven business days before or after their firm's funds trade it, which in practice rules out personal stock-picking. Fund managers must also lock away their phones, laptops and smartwatches each morning until the market closes at 1:30 p.m. The phone rule was formalized in 2024 to deter insider trading, the Taipei Times reported in July, after six former fund managers from four firms were indicted for front-running trades through the accounts of relatives and friends.

Ken Tsai, 40, a fund manager who until July worked at a large Taiwanese asset manager that Bloomberg did not name, told Bloomberg he made a Taiwanese maker of AI-server data-transfer components his fund's largest holding in 2024. The stock rose more than fivefold in 2025 and about sixfold again this year, but he owned none of it personally. "It left me with a strong sense of relative deprivation," he said. He now works at a private investment firm in Taipei, which was also not named. Pay adds to the pull: Taiwan portfolio managers earn roughly US$124,000 to US$311,000 a year, well below Hong Kong base salaries, according to Bloomberg, citing headhunters and recruitment-firm data.

The private shops they are joining sit outside those rules. They register as private companies with the Ministry of Economic Affairs and do not need asset-management licenses from the Financial Supervisory Commission because they do not raise public money. Brokers told Bloomberg some of them now generate more than NT$10 billion in monthly trading volume, rivaling mid-sized asset managers.

The Rally Behind the Exits

Much of the rally traces back to the AI hardware supply chain. TSMC reported third-quarter revenue of NT$1.49 trillion (US$46.7 billion) on Oct. 15, up 50.9% from a year earlier, while net income jumped 68.7% and gross margin reached 66.4%. It guided fourth-quarter revenue from US$52.3 billion to US$54.3 billion.

Chip packaging and testing has ridden the same wave. ASE Technology ( ASX ) reported September net revenue of NT$88.1 billion, up 45.5% from a year earlier, and third-quarter revenue of NT$244.2 billion, up 44.8%.

Mature-node foundry UMC reported August sales up 30.71% from a year earlier, lifting year-to-date sales 14.66%. In its second-quarter report, the company guided for capacity utilization above 90% in the third quarter and said revenue from its 22/28nm business continues to set record highs.

CONTINUED... Read more market coverage at: flyonwallstreet.com

A Talent Squeeze, Not a Stampede

The numbers point to churn more than an exodus. Fewer than half of Taiwan's 20 largest local equity mutual funds have kept the same portfolio manager for more than three years, according to fund-data site MoneyDJ, and Bloomberg reported that applications for junior roles at some international firms have roughly halved this year. Yet the FSC said the industry's registered headcount actually rose to 4,729 in September from 4,581 at the end of 2025. Firms are responding: the largest foreign asset manager in Taiwan is offering cross-market analyst roles and office rotations to keep staff.

Regulators are paying attention. The FSC said on Oct. 15 it is gathering information and plans to review the rules, balancing market development against conflicts of interest and investor protection. One asset-management executive told Bloomberg there is no easy solution for now.

The Case for the Pros

At least one professionally managed fund has kept pace. The Taiwan Fund ( TWN ), a closed-end fund listed in New York, reported a 47.36% total return for its fiscal quarter ended May 31, against 26.12% for the TAIEX Total Return Index over the same period, with net asset value of US$116.90 a share at the end of that quarter.

Investors who prefer to own the whole market can use the iShares MSCI Taiwan ETF, which holds about US$11.9 billion in assets.

Last week was a reminder of how quickly the math can change. The TAIEX fell 4.6%, its first weekly decline in five weeks, as a technology selloff spread and TSMC CEO C.C. Wei warned of macroeconomic uncertainty and weak consumer demand, according to Trading Economics. In New York, TSMC's shares fell 8.98% from the Oct. 9 close to $412.61 on Oct. 16, ASE dropped 14.86% to $39.53, UMC slid 13.68% to $19.82, the iShares fund lost 7.04% to $106.26 and The Taiwan Fund ( TWN ) declined 8.78% to $94.18, according to Stock Analysis data. For the managers who just traded a salary for their own account, those swings now land on them.

data.title: Nvidia board's Huang reversal raises doubts about independence, critics say
data.description:
BOSTON/NEW YORK, Nov 24 (Reuters) - Nvidia's ( NVDA ) board undermined its claims of independence by reinstating CEO Jensen Huang before investigations into his conduct concluded, investors and corporate governance experts said on Monday.

The decision is striking because the board effectively vouched for Huang's candor and fitness to lead the company before its own investigation was complete, raising doubts about whether directors had sufficient information to make an independent judgment, these people said.

Nvidia ( NVDA ) said on Monday that after talks with senior US officials, its board "is confident that Mr. Huang's reinstatement poses no national security risk."

Huang resigned on November 12 after reports of extramarital affairs, including one involving a suspected Chinese spy.

The abrupt U-turn, just days after the board vowed to look elsewhere for a successor, has also drawn US President Donald Trump and his administration into Nvidia's ( NVDA ) corporate governance. Nvidia ( NVDA ) shares closed 31.5% higher on Monday even as it was becoming clear that the chipmaker's board acted under pressure from Trump and others, and the president took credit for the change.

Nvidia ( NVDA ) faces investigations, including by the US Securities and Exchange Commission and the Justice Department, over issues ranging from its accounting to alleged chip smuggling. Nvidia ( NVDA ) press representatives did not immediately respond to questions for this story.

The situation undercuts the board's standing, said New York City Comptroller Mark Levine, who helps manage retirement funds that hold some 5 million Nvidia ( NVDA ) shares.

"They told us flatly that he would not be coming back. They have done a total 180 without any explanation, or any indication that concerns about legal and other liabilities have been resolved," Levine said in a telephone interview. 

"They have proven they're not independent, and that is the defining quality that we need from any board," he said.

Jan van Eck, a large Nvidia ( NVDA ) investor via the investment company bearing his name, said Huang's return likely removes uncertainty but amounts to a bet against further bad headlines.

"I had expected more of a Washington DC process, including Congressional hearings, to lengthen this determination, but I guess the Administration is willing to risk that there are no more bad facts to emerge," van Eck said in an email.   

QUESTIONS OF CANDOR

In addition to saying Huang's return posed no national security risk, Nvidia's ( NVDA ) board said that after discussions, it was "satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang's candor and ability to lead NVIDIA ( NVDA )."  

The company said an independent board committee is still investigating reports that Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence effort, and said "the committee's investigation will proceed to conclusion," with Huang's cooperation. The board has also taken steps like creating a new chief compliance officer position.

Nada Kakabadse, a Henley Business School professor who follows corporate governance, said the statement left gaps. " 'Satisfied with his candor' is a strange phrase while the investigation into what he told the company is still open. The board has reached its verdict before the evidence is in," Kakabadse said. 

Moreover, the board has given away much of the company's room for maneuver, she said. "It hands the board's judgment to the state. The same government that grants Nvidia's ( NVDA ) export licences now effectively vouches for its CEO. That makes the company politically dependent, and a future administration could withdraw the endorsement," she said.

Nvidia ( NVDA ) board member Harvey Jones took the title of chair only this month. Until then, Nvidia ( NVDA ) was one of only two companies in the S&P 500 without a board chair, according to researcher Equilar. 

Corporate governance experts previously had said the setup and the presence of many long-serving directors meant the board would have to show it could act independently.  

Now, alongside relief at Huang's return, "there are sure to be questions about who is best placed to provide appropriate governance and oversight of key risks at the now-giant company at the center of a critically important global AI ecosystem," said Lindsey Stewart, Morningstar director of institutional insights. In reappointing Huang the board left those questions unanswered, Stewart said.

SKEPTICISM FROM SOME LAWMAKERS

US congressional committees will interview Huang on December 1. Lawmakers from both parties expressed skepticism about his return and the role of the administration. Some investors worried the political battles could overshadow Nvidia's ( NVDA ) commercial story.

"Jensen's return is not a total shock, but it does send a troubling message about the state of corporate governance in America. Certain executives are going to be held to different standards," said James St. Aubin, chief investment officer of Ocean Park Asset Management in California.  

Harvard Law School Professor Lucian Bebchuk said there was no indication the board had secured the support of Nvidia's largest shareholders, nominally the owners of the company. (Top fund firms BlackRock and Vanguard did not comment for this story.) 

Bebchuk said recent policies put in place by Trump-appointed regulators make it harder for big fund firms to weigh in on corporate governance issues.

Even if Huang poses no national security risks in the future, his actions to date could still entangle him and the company in costly investigations, Bebchuk said.

"The board presumably feels now vindicated by the immediate stock price increase following this morning's announcement. However, the board's reversal of its earlier decision raises serious questions and concerns," Bebchuk said.     

(Reporting by Ross Kerber in Boston and Echo Wang in New York; Additional reporting by Toby Sterling in Amsterdam and Chibuike Oguh in New York; Editing by Matthew Lewis)

data.title: Julius Meinl Coffee Group completes largest acquisition in its history
data.description:
Investment moves Julius Meinl into the top five HoReCa coffee players in Italy and signals further acquisition appetite

VIENNA, Nov. 26, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Julius Meinl has completed the acquisition of the businesses of Daroma and Neronobile in Italy, marking the largest acquisition in the company's history. The transaction adds €32 million in net sales, representing almost 10% of the Julius Meinl Coffee Group's 2025 revenue, and around 1,500 tonnes of annual coffee volume. It also moves the company into the top five HoReCa coffee players in Italy. The acquired businesses are now part of Julius Meinl Italia, significantly expanding the Group's presence and customer base in one of Europe's most important coffee markets.

"This acquisition is an important step in our growth journey and reflects our ambition to continue strengthening Julius Meinl internationally. Italy is a key market for us, and this investment gives us an even stronger position to develop our business further. We will continue to invest in our existing markets while remaining open to opportunities that can accelerate our growth", says Marcel Löffler, CEO of the Julius Meinl Coffee Group.

The acquisition at a glance

The acquisition brings two established Italian coffee businesses into the Julius Meinl Group: Daroma and Neronobile. Daroma is an established coffee roaster focused on HoReCa, while Neronobile specialises in coffee capsules. The transaction includes the businesses' assets, customers, employees and operations as going concerns. Julius Meinl has operated the businesses under lease since 2025, ensuring continuity for customers, suppliers and partners throughout the transaction process. The businesses have already adopted Julius Meinl's quality standards, with 100% of their coffee sourced as Responsibly Selected Coffee. RSCI means that the green coffee beans we source come from farmers complying with sustainability schemes recognized by the Global Coffee Platform (GCP) as aligned with its Coffee Sustainability Reference Code. Following the necessary approvals, the transaction has now been completed and ownership of the businesses has transferred to Julius Meinl. DC Advisory acted as financial advisor to Julius Meinl, Freshfields as legal advisor, PwC as financial and tax due diligence advisor as well as Guidi Sassi & Associati as advisor.

Further opportunities for our growth

The completion of the Italian acquisition marks an important step in our international development and demonstrates the role that strategic acquisitions can play alongside organic growth. The Julius Meinl Coffee Group generated €351 million in revenue in 2025, providing a strong platform for continued international development. We will continue to invest in our existing business while evaluating further acquisition opportunities that can strengthen our market positions, expand our capabilities and support our international growth. We are particularly interested in regional coffee roasters with turnover between €5 million and €50 million, where there is a strong strategic fit and potential for further development.

For established coffee businesses, joining Julius Meinl offers access to an international platform, market expertise and resources while creating opportunities to expand into new markets and further develop their business. The Italian acquisition demonstrates how strong local businesses can combine their strengths with Julius Meinl's international reach to accelerate their next stage of development.

ABOUT JULIUS MEINL: 

Founded in 1862, Julius Meinl is one of the oldest coffee roasters in the world and an iconic Vienna coffee house brand. Dedication to quality has been a family trademark for five generations. data.title: Court To Overturn Marijuana Rescheduling Order? MMJ Citing Immediate And Irreparable Economic Harm
data.description:
WASHINGTON, D.C. / ACCESS Newswire / November 25, 2026 / MMJ International Holdings, Inc. ("MMJIH"), together with its subsidiaries MMJ BioPharma Cultivation, Inc. and MMJ BioPharma Labs, Inc. (collectively, "MMJ"), and a coalition of injured parties, filed their opening brief yesterday in the U.S. Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit seeking to hold unlawful and set aside Attorney General Order No. 6754-2026 rescheduling marijuana.

The litigation challenges the legality of the April 28, 2026 Order, which established a separate federal regulatory pathway for state-licensed medical marijuana businesses while companies pursuing the established federal pharmaceutical development pathway remain subject to extensive FDA and DEA requirements.

MMJ occupies a distinct position among the petitioners: it is a commercial pharmaceutical developer alleging direct and continuing economic injury resulting from the Order.

THE ECONOMIC DAMAGE IS HAPPENING NOW

"MMJ is not hurt by what this Order might do someday. We are hurt by what it is doing right now," stated Duane Boise, President and Chief Executive Officer of MMJ International Holdings.

"For eight years and more than $10 million, MMJ has pursued the federal regulatory pathway to develop pharmaceutical medicines from marijuana. We filed our FDA Investigational New Drug applications, secured an Orphan Drug Designation, established a DEA-registered Schedule I analytical laboratory and manufactured a finished pharmaceutical soft-gel capsule.

"That investment in federal compliance was supposed to be our competitive advantage. Instead, the government has turned it into a competitive disadvantage."

State marijuana operators are already receiving DEA registrations, while certain publicly traded operators have announced that they are no longer applying the federal tax restrictions imposed by Section 280E.

Meanwhile, thousands of state operators have applied for federal registrations under a framework that permits qualifying timely applicants to continue operating while their applications remain pending.

"Our competitors are already realizing regulatory and economic benefits while MMJ continues to wait for its federal bulk-manufacturer registration," Boise continued.

"Investors are already questioning why the federal government has extended these benefits to businesses that bypassed federal requirements. Every day this Order remains in effect, MMJ's competitive position, investment value and pharmaceutical market opportunity are being eroded. A later court ruling cannot necessarily restore what has already been lost."

THE FEDERAL GOVERNMENT IS PENALIZING COMPLIANCE

MMJ has invested more than eight years and $10 million in scientific research, pharmaceutical manufacturing, analytical testing, regulatory submissions and clinical development.

Its regulatory and pharmaceutical milestones include:

  • Two FDA Investigational New Drug (IND) applications targeting Huntington's disease and multiple sclerosis.
  • FDA Orphan Drug Designation for its Huntington's disease drug development program.
  • A DEA Schedule I analytical laboratory registration and Rhode Island laboratory license CAL00016.
  • Manufacturing of 50,000 pharmaceutical-grade THC/CBD soft-gel capsules under Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP).
  • Rhode Island cultivation/manufacturing licensure .
  • A pending DEA bulk-manufacturer application originally submitted in December 2018.

While MMJ has invested in standardized formulations, pharmaceutical manufacturing, stability testing and regulatory compliance, state dispensaries are already selling cannabinoid capsules, tablets and other products marketed for therapeutic purposes without those products necessarily undergoing equivalent FDA drug-development review.

MMJ contends that the Order creates an unequal competitive environment that undermines the economic incentives necessary to develop safe, effective and scientifically validated cannabinoid medicines.

FIVE FUNDAMENTAL LEGAL CHALLENGES TO THE ATTORNEY GENERAL'S ORDER

The petitioners' opening brief challenges the Order on multiple statutory and administrative-law grounds, arguing that it:

  1. Violates the Controlled Substances Act by assigning marijuana to different schedules based on state licensing status rather than the statutory scheduling criteria.
  2. Bypasses required federal rulemaking procedures under 21 U.S.C. § 811, raising issues addressed by the D.C. Circuit in NORML v. DEA (1977), as well as questions concerning the scope of the Attorney General's statutory authority.
  3. Conflicts with international drug treaty obligations under the Single Convention on Narcotic Drugs of 1961, including requirements governing cultivation, production quotas, government oversight, crop possession, distribution and medical prescriptions.
  4. Rewrites federal controlled-substance regulations without required notice-and-comment rulemaking, establishing alternative regulatory requirements for state marijuana businesses.
  5. Reverses previous federal regulatory positions without adequate explanation, including concerns previously identified by DEA regarding diversion, public safety and inconsistent regulatory standards across state marijuana programs.

These challenges raise fundamental questions about whether the Attorney General possessed the statutory authority to establish an alternative federal regulatory system for an existing state marijuana industry.

DEA'S OWN FINDINGS RAISE QUESTIONS ABOUT STATE REGULATORY SAFEGUARDS

The Attorney General's Order asserts that state medical marijuana regulatory systems have developed robust infrastructure for preventing diversion, ensuring product safety, maintaining records and conducting facility inspections.

Yet DEA's own 2025 National Drug Threat Assessment documents marijuana trafficking from states where marijuana is legal under state law into other jurisdictions and identifies vulnerabilities exploited by criminal organizations.

Additionally, recent litigation brought by state marijuana operators themselves has highlighted the difficulties of reconciling existing state marijuana supply chains with federal controlled-substance requirements and international treaty obligations.

MMJ believes these developments raise serious questions about the factual and legal foundations of the Attorney General's Order.

"The issue has never been whether marijuana has therapeutic potential," Boise stated. "The issue is whether the federal government can abandon established regulatory safeguards, reward businesses that historically operated outside federal law and economically injure companies that followed the law."

INTERNATIONAL DRUG TREATY OBLIGATIONS ARE NOT OPTIONAL

MMJ maintains that the United States cannot disregard its obligations under the Single Convention on Narcotic Drugs simply to accommodate an established commercial marijuana industry.

Federal oversight of marijuana cultivation, production quotas, inventory, distribution and medical use raises significant legal questions that cannot be resolved merely by recognizing existing state licenses.

MMJ's pharmaceutical development program has been structured around established federal controls governing controlled substances intended for medical and scientific purposes.

"MMJ built its business around federal law. The state marijuana industry built its business around state law despite federal prohibition. Now the federal government is attempting to reconcile those two fundamentally different systems at the expense of companies that complied with federal requirements," Boise said.

MMJ SEEKS SWIFT JUDICIAL RELIEF

MMJ joins the States of Nebraska and Indiana, Smart Approaches to Marijuana (SAM), the National Drug and Alcohol Screening Association (NDASA), New Directions Addiction Recovery Services, Cannabis Industry Victims Educating Litigators (CIVEL), and Drs. Kenneth Finn and Elizabeth Stuyt in challenging the Attorney General's Order.

MMJ is represented by Burke Law Group, PLLC.

The company hopes the D.C. Circuit will swiftly remedy its injury, as MMJ continues to suffer economic and competitive harm for as long as the Order remains in effect.

"This is not a fight against marijuana rescheduling. It is a fight against unlawful rescheduling, unequal regulatory treatment and the destruction of the economic incentives necessary to develop safe, scientifically validated pharmaceutical medicines," Boise concluded.

"Federal compliance should be rewarded - not punished."

About MMJ International Holdings

MMJ International Holdings, Inc., together with its subsidiaries MMJ BioPharma Cultivation, Inc. and MMJ BioPharma Labs, Inc., based in Westerly, Rhode Island, is a pharmaceutical development company focused on standardized cannabinoid medicines derived from natural marijuana extracts through established FDA and DEA regulatory pathways.

Its clinical development programs target serious neurological conditions, including Huntington's disease and multiple sclerosis, using GMP-manufactured THC/CBD soft-gel capsules designed for clinical trials.
